extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of literary criticism; readers learning to do close readings of poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for close-reading and evaluating poems, emphasising how to detect sense, feeling, tone, intention, versification, and common reading errors. Aimed at teaching principled critical judgement rather than subjective reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense (Function 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine what the poem is saying — the propositions, references, and items for consideration the words present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish accurate comprehension of the poem's sense before judging other aspects. Many misreadings arise from failure to master the sense; disentangle metre and other distractions, and be prepared to do several readings. Avoid reducing the poem to a prose paraphrase as the sole test of its value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeling (Function 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the feelings or affective attitudes the poem expresses or aims to evoke about its subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that many poetic statements serve primarily emotive ends; evaluate whether the feelings are effectively communicated. Do not mistake emotive expression for factual claims; attend to emotional nuance and whether the poem justifies deviations in sense to serve feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone (Function 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the poem's attitude toward its audience — the manner, register, and social stance in which it addresses readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how diction and conversational touches (e.g., 'rude question') position the speaker relative to the reader. Tone affects reception; evaluate whether tone is appropriate to intention and subject. Beware mistaking a conversational or urbane tone for insincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intention (Function 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the poet's purpose or aim (conscious or unconscious) — what the poem is trying to do or achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimating intention is part of judging success; intentions may govern arrangement, emphasis, and 'hiding the hand.' Intention often operates through the other three functions and must be considered to assess whether means are warranted by ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of Means to Ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the poem's formal means (diction, metre, rhythm, figures) are rightly subordinated to its ends (sense, feeling, tone, intention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether apparent faults (irregular metre, nonsense, logical irrelevance) are justified by their service to feeling or intention. Good criticism inspects whether form supports purpose, not merely whether it conforms to external rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware Stock Responses and Personal Associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid letting habitual or popular reactions, or personal associations with other poets, dictate interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set aside automatic labels (e.g., 'sanctimonious', comparisons to known authors) and test them against textual evidence. Personal distressing associations are not grounds for objective criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Readings Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Most poetry requires several readings for its varied factors (sense, rhythm, feeling) to cohere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't accept a first-impression verdict; reread to disentangle competing influences (metre, syntax, sound) and to let the poem's complexity emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Careless 'Intuitive' Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on a single intuitive flash that dismisses the poem without analytic scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careless guessing about sense or motive is unreliable; check syntax and literal sense before moving to higher-level judgments. The 'intuition' excuse is often a cover for insufficient effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Over-literal Prosaic Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not judge a poem solely by a plain prose paraphrase of its statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many poetic statements function for emotive or tonal effect rather than factual contribution; reducing them to prose doctrine misses their purpose. Balance attention to sense with recognition of figurative and emotive uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Statements Meant for Emotive Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise when lines are not claims of truth but devices to manipulate feeling (metaphor, hyperbole, logical irrelevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a statement is logically odd or factually false, evaluate whether it is serving feeling or tone. Logical nonsense can be permissible when it furthers the poem's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meter and Versification — Pattern and Irregularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse the poem's metrical pattern (syllable counts, line lengths, stanza patterns) and whether irregularities are confusing or effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count syllables and note recurrent patterns; determine whether irregularities are accidental, clumsy, or deliberate. Consider examples given (varying 7-, 8-, 9-, 10-syllable lines) and whether irregularities displease the ear or serve a purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and Stress Alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the natural rhythmic flow — whether sense-stresses coincide with metrical stresses and whether lines read comfortably without forced elision or misaccentuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check lines for awkward readings (e.g., 'to attend' forced to 'attend'), for misplacements that jar or tire. Distinguish between metrically regular but tired patterns and genuinely disruptive derangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosodic Effect on Sense and Feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how versification and rhythm affect the poem's semantic and emotive delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether tricky metre distracts from sense or whether sound patterns (lilt, lurch, 'caw' for rhyme) illuminate tone or meaning. The interconnection of form and content must be carefully weighed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-choice and Small Dictional Shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the significance of single words or phrases (e.g., 'rude') in setting tone and guiding interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single word may be pivotal to the poem's tone (conversational vs rebuke). Investigate its range of senses and place in the 'texture' of the poem before condemning it as frivolous or inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity vs Affected Naiveté
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the poem's manner is genuinely felt or an affected, mock-naïf pose intended to provoke a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs of contrivance: inconsistent form, gratuitous simplicity, or rhetorical affectation. But allow that apparent naiveté may be deliberate artifice (parody) and judge it by its success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting Maudlin or Sentimental Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify when a poem is mawkish, cheaply sentimental, or emotionally overwrought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether sentimentality is warranted by subject and whether meter, diction, and imagery rise above 'gush.' Examples: 'foolish pomp of this world of ours' or 'richest and rarest of all dowers' as potential gush; assess whether expansion serves a catalogue effect or is mere redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy and Expansion Versus Conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether repetitions or amplifications add necessary emphasis (catalogue effect) or merely bloat the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansion can be a deliberate device to make the obvious more manifest; assess the rhetorical function (e.g., turning phrase into a list) before labelling it redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Genre/Contextual Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust critical expectations according to genre (scientific treatise, popular exposition, political speech, meditative poem) because different functions dominate in different genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, popularisation may trade precision of sense for intelligibility and tone; political speech will privilege intention and feeling over factual presentation. Apply the four functions with different weights per context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Close Structural Faults from Reader's Presuppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert that complaints about form or movement often stem from a reader's presupposed interpretation of sense or emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace whether a prosodic complaint (bogged redundancy, muddy time) depends on an initial misreading of sense; re-evaluate form after considering alternate sense/tone readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware Rhetorical/Emotive Projection
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid attributing motives or moral character to the poet or speaker based on hostile emotional reaction (e.g., calling poet a prig, fanatic, or neurotic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test emotionally charged judgments against textual evidence of intention and tone. Personal invective rarely substitutes for analytic critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of Technical Prosodic Commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, apply technical prosodic analysis (syllable counts, line-by-line metrical accounting) to substantiate judgements about versification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prosodic detail to show where irregularities occur and whether they are confusing or pleasing; but weigh such technical findings within broader interpretive context (sense, tone, intention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody, Irony and Intentional Mismatch of Form and Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise that deliberate mismatch (frivolous rhythm with solemn theme) can be a conscious device (parody, pastiche) rather than an artistic fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether apparent insincerity or mock simplicity functions as parody (e.g., echoing a sermonic form to comic effect). If intention fits the device, judge by success rather than conformity to seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 'Simplegades' — avoid two twin errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the twin dangers of (a) careless, intuitive reading that guesses meaning, and (b) over-literal prosaic reading that strips poetic function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigate between these extremes: do careful syntactic/sense work without obliterating figurative, emotive, and tonal functions. Both errors commonly wreck understanding.
